## Aims and data

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Aims**

- Describe red mullet (*Mullus barbatus*) **biomass in space and time** in two areas
- Express **habitat suitability on a 0-1 scale**
- Then relate it to **fishing effort** and marine heatwaves

**Data decisions**

- Response: **biomass** (kg/km²) per MEDITS haul
- **2014-2021**: no Croatian MEDITS survey in 2012-2013 (also avoids the early AIS ramp-up)
- Bottom temperature, salinity, oxygen and SST matched to each haul (Copernicus)
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
[`r num(k$grp_hauls[["GSA 6"]])`]{.big-number}
[valid hauls, GSA 6 (northern Spain)]{.big-label}
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
[`r num(k$grp_hauls[["GSAs 17-18"]])`]{.big-number}
[valid hauls, GSAs 17-18 (Adriatic)]{.big-label}
:::
::::

Red mullet absent from `r pc(k$grp_absent[["GSA 6"]])` of GSA 6 hauls and `r pc(k$grp_absent[["GSAs 17-18"]])` of Adriatic hauls.

::: {.caveat}
Two thin years: GSA 6 in **2020** (`r k$grp_thin_6` hauls, COVID-19) and the Adriatic in **2017** (`r k$grp_thin_1718` hauls).
:::
:::
::::

## The model: sdmTMB

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
The fitting script is not shared yet, so the structure is **reconstructed from the saved predictions**:

<p style="text-align:center; font-size:1.15em; margin:1.2em 0;">log(biomass) = **depth + bottom temperature** + **ω** (spatial) + **ε** (spatio-temporal, by year)</p>

- Fixed effects exactly linear (R² = 1 when refitted), **no year effect**
- Year-to-year change comes only from **bottom temperature** and **ε**
- Family and mesh not recoverable from the predictions
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
| | GSA 6 | GSAs 17-18 |
|---|---|---|
| Per +100 m depth | −`r pc(k$grp_depth_drop[["GSA 6"]])` | −`r pc(k$grp_depth_drop[["GSAs 17-18"]])` |
| Per +1 °C bottom temp. | `r pcs(k$grp_temp_rise[["GSA 6"]])` | `r pcs(k$grp_temp_rise[["GSAs 17-18"]])` |
| Largest \|ε\| | `r num(k$grp_eps_max[["GSA 6"]], 0.1)` | `r num(k$grp_eps_max[["GSAs 17-18"]], 0.1)` |

[Change in predicted biomass per unit of each covariate, on the response scale.]{.small .muted}
:::
::::

## Predicted biomass: Adriatic

![](figures/fig-grp-dens-1718-1.png){width="88%" fig-align="center"}

[Highest in the shallow northern basin and along the Croatian coast; a gentler depth gradient over a much wider shelf.]{.small .muted}

## Spatial and spatio-temporal random effects

![](figures/fig-grp-eps-1.png){width="100%" fig-align="center"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**ω** (first column): persistent hotspots not explained by depth and temperature
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**ε** by year: small in GSA 6, large in the Adriatic (up to ±`r num(k$grp_eps_max[["GSAs 17-18"]], 0.1)`, a factor of ~`r round(exp(k$grp_eps_max[["GSAs 17-18"]]))` in biomass)
:::
::::

## Biomass index

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
![](figures/fig-grp-index-1.png){width="100%"}
:::
::: {.column width="42%"}
Sum of predicted biomass × cell area, per year

[`r pcs(k$grp_idx_6_change)`]{.big-number}
[GSA 6, 2015 → 2021 (Tweedie GAM of Section 2b: `r pcs(k$grp_gam_change / 100)` in density)]{.big-label}

[`r pc(k$grp_idx_1718_rng[1])`-`r pc(k$grp_idx_1718_rng[2])`]{.big-number}
[Adriatic, range relative to its mean]{.big-label}

::: {.caveat}
Each area peaks in its **least-sampled year**. Index standard errors (`get_index()`) need the fitted model.
:::
:::
::::

## Extrapolation in GSA 6

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
[`r pc(k$grp_shallow_cells)`]{.big-number}
[of the GSA 6 grid is shallower than the shallowest haul (`r k$grp_min_depth` m)]{.big-label}
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
[`r pc(k$grp_shallow_bio)`]{.big-number}
[of predicted GSA 6 biomass sits in those cells]{.big-label}
:::
::::

::: {.caveat}
Linear effects (biomass ↑ with temperature, ↓ with depth) push the shallowest, warmest coastal cells beyond the sampled range. **Restrict the prediction grid to the sampled depth range.**
:::

## Habitat suitability index (HSI)

![](figures/fig-grp-hsi-1.png){width="100%" fig-align="center"}

[Fixed effects (depth + bottom temperature) rescaled to 0-1 across all years in each area; reproduces the group's maps. Highest on the shallow inner shelf; in the Adriatic, the northern basin scores high almost everywhere.]{.small .muted}

## Change in habitat suitability, 2014 to 2021

![](figures/fig-grp-perc-1.png){width="80%" fig-align="center"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- GSA 6: median **`r pcs(k$grp_perc_med[["GSA 6"]] / 100, 0.1)`**, almost no change
- Adriatic: median **`r pcs(k$grp_perc_med[["GSAs 17-18"]] / 100, 0.1)`**; `r pc(k$grp_hsi_lower[["GSAs 17-18"]])` of cells lose suitability, mainly the northern basin
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.caveat}
% change of a 0-1 index explodes where HSI ≈ 0 (up to `r pcs(k$grp_perc_max_6 / 100)` in one GSA 6 cell): use the **difference in HSI** and a **2014-2021 trend** rather than two years.
:::
:::
::::

## Overlap between red mullet and trawling

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
![](data/group/correlation_map_2700.jpeg){width="100%"}
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
Local correlation between red mullet and **GFW trawling effort**, by year

- **Red**: trawling concentrated where red mullet is abundant
- GSA 6: mostly negative, positive patches on the outer shelf
- Adriatic: a positive band through the north-western and central basin every year; coastal edge negative

::: {.caveat}
Method not yet shared (variables, window). In small windows, correlations near ±1 are common by chance: add a **significance test** or a **whole-area overlap measure**.
:::
:::
::::

## Next steps

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**To share**

1. sdmTMB fitting script (mesh, family, formula)
2. Data preparation (`MB_*`, effort and prediction grids)
3. HSI rescaling (to confirm)
4. Correlation-map script
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**To improve**

- Index **standard errors**, especially for thin years
- Prediction grid within the **sampled depth range**
- HSI change as a **difference or trend**, not % between two years
- Overlap with trawling: **significance** and a single summary per area and year
:::
